title: Maximum evidence maturity does not transfer execution authority

ideaContract.purpose: Export independently inspectable review evidence without transferring or implying execution authority.
ideaContract.expectedOutcome: Downstream ProofPath/CML consumers receive evidence state plus an explicit negative authority contract.
invariants: evidence may inform a separate authorization decision but never grants authority by itself
maximum review maturity does not grant execution capability
downstream consumers must not infer authority from omitted fields
forbiddenOutcomes: execution authority inferred from review maturity
capability grant inferred from EEW or VALIDATED status
ideaContract.parentContract: LiminalOSAI AUTHORIZATION remains a distinct causal contract from external review evidence.

evidence.claim: FCRP-SELF-009 was promoted after exact-head Core CI, Governance Required Gate, and External Validation Graph Gate passed.
The export requires EVIDENCE_ONLY classification, zero authority transfer, and a separate authorization contract even when EEW is 100/100.

past.summary: Historical cross-repository mappings carried review state and evidence without a mandatory machine-readable negative authorization fact.

present.summary: LiminalOSAI main exports explicit non-authorizing evidence semantics after FCRP-SELF-009.

future.summary: Every downstream system consumes evidence and authority as separate contracts rather than inferring capability from evidence maturity.

causalPath.statement: The historical export shape omitted a mandatory negative authorization contract.
A downstream consumer could be forced to infer whether mature evidence had authority implications.
Export explicit EVIDENCE_ONLY semantics, zero authority transfer, and require a separate authorization contract.
Maximum review maturity remains non-authorizing and portable across repository boundaries.

navigation.reason: The local evidence graph was conservative; the missing guarantee existed at the parent cross-repository authority contract.

refactor.change: Make the negative authority boundary machine-readable at the evidence export boundary.
refactor.expectedEffect: Evidence strength can increase without silently increasing execution authority.

authorization.authorityBoundary: This portability case evaluates a contract only; it grants no permission to mutate LiminalOSAI, ProofPath, CML, or any external system.
